_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Sweden covering Viking Age (8th-11th century, raids/trade, founded Rus'), Christianization 11th century, Kalmar Union 1397-1523, Vasa dynasty, Swedish Empire (stormaktstiden 17th century, Gustav II Adolf Thirty Years War), Great Northern War (1700-21, lost Baltic supremacy to Russia), neutrality policy (since 1815, 200+ years), industrialization, Nobel Prize, social-democratic welfare state (folkhem), EU 1995, NATO 2024 (historic shift post-Ukraine invasion).

religion.note: Church of Sweden (Lutheran, state church until 2000, membership 53% but attendance ~2%); highly secularized society (among most secular in world); Islam (immigration 1970s+, Syrian refugees 2015, ~820k); free church tradition (Baptist, Pentecostal); religious freedom 1951

ethnic_groups.name: Swedish
ethnic_groups.notes: Germanic/Norse; Viking heritage; Protestant work ethic; lagom (moderation/balance, neither too much nor too little); Jante Law (social conformity, anti-boastfulness); consensus culture; reserved but egalitarian; welfare state pride

ethnic_groups.name: Syrian
ethnic_groups.notes: ~190k (2015 refugee crisis, most per capita in Europe, integration challenges, segregated suburbs, 2022 Quran burnings tensions)

ethnic_groups.name: Iraqi
ethnic_groups.notes: ~135k (1990s-2000s wars, largest Iraqi diaspora per capita)

ethnic_groups.name: Finnish
ethnic_groups.notes: Tornedalians (Finnish-speaking, Norrbotten, Meänkieli language); historical Swedish territory (Finland until 1809)

ethnic_groups.name: Somali
ethnic_groups.notes: ~70k (civil war refugees, 1990s+, integration struggles, gang violence issues)

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Polish (~50k, labor migration), Iranian (~70k, 1980s), Bosnian (~60k, Yugoslav Wars), Eritrean, Afghan, Turkish; Sami indigenous (~20-40k, reindeer herding, Sapmi, 5 languages, parliament since 1993); Romani (~50k); foreign-born 20% of population (highest in Nordic countries, immigration debate central since 2010s, gang violence crisis 2020s)

country_profile.notes_unique: Swedish welfare state model (folkhemmet 'people's home', social democracy, universal healthcare/education, parental leave 480 days, high taxes ~50%, gender equality policies, Olof Palme architect); neutrality (200+ years, since 1815, not invaded since 1814, WWII neutral but transited German troops to Norway, controversial, sold iron ore to Nazis); NATO 2024 (historic shift, abandoned neutrality after Russia invaded Ukraine, application 2022, Türkiye delayed, acceded March 2024); Nobel Prize (Alfred Nobel, Stockholm awards, Peace Prize in Oslo but Swedish Academy, Literature/Physics/Chemistry/Medicine/Economics); ABBA (1970s, Eurovision 1974, global phenomenon); IKEA (flat-pack furniture, Swedish design aesthetic, Billy bookshelf); Volvo (safety reputation); H&M, Spotify; Pippi Longstocking (Astrid Lindgren); Greta Thunberg (climate activism); Stieg Larsson (Millennium trilogy); Vikings (founded Rus' in Russia/Ukraine, raided/traded Europe, runes, sagas); Vasa Museum (warship sank 1628, recovered 1961); Midsummer (major celebration); fika (coffee break culture); Gang violence crisis (2020s, shootings/bombings, highest gun deaths in Europe 2022, blamed on failed integration, segregated suburbs, organized crime); Swedish Academy (Nobel Literature, #MeToo scandal 2018); Right to public access (allemansrätten, free roaming in nature); carbon negative goal 2045

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Ulf Kristersson
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Moderate Party (center-right); coalition with Christian Democrats/Liberals; parliamentary support from Sweden Democrats (far-right, anti-immigration, 2nd largest party, kingmakers but not in government); ended 8 years of Social Democrat rule; tougher on immigration/crime; NATO application (historic policy shift); addresses gang violence crisis

head_of_state.name: King Carl XVI Gustaf
head_of_state.title: King of Sweden
head_of_state.notes: Bernadotte dynasty; longest-reigning Swedish monarch; constitutional monarch (no political power since 1975); married Queen Silvia (Brazilian-German); children: Crown Princess Victoria (heir), Prince Carl Philip, Princess Madeleine; popular; dyslexia advocate

former_leaders.name: Magdalena Andersson
former_leaders.notes: Social Democrats; first female PM; PM twice (resigned after hours, re-elected, served 1 year); finance minister; lost 2022 election (SD surge); competent but brief tenure

former_leaders.name: Stefan Löfven
former_leaders.notes: Social Democrats; welder/union leader; PM 7 years; 2015 refugee crisis (163k asylum seekers, highest per capita, border controls imposed); coalition challenges; pragmatic

former_leaders.name: Fredrik Reinfeldt
former_leaders.notes: Moderate Party; center-right; Alliance coalition; financial crisis response; open-door immigration (humanitarian superpower rhetoric); EU fiscal compact; modernized party

former_leaders.name: Göran Persson
former_leaders.notes: Social Democrats; 10 years; rejected Euro 2003 referendum; welfare reforms; Tsunami 2004 (543 Swedes killed Thailand, government criticized for slow response)

former_leaders.name: Olof Palme
former_leaders.notes: Social Democrats; charismatic; welfare state architect; anti-Vietnam War (US relations strained); anti-apartheid; assassinated February 28, 1986 (Stockholm street, unsolved for 34 years, Stig Engström suspected 2020 but deceased, still no definitive closure); martyred, defines an era

former_leaders.name: Tage Erlander
former_leaders.notes: Social Democrats; 23 years PM (record); built welfare state; neutrality/Third Way; Social Democratic golden age

910.name: Prehistoric Sweden & Vendel Era
910.description: Sweden's prehistory from post-glacial settlement through the Nordic Bronze Age, the Iron Age, and the splendid Vendel Era with its warrior aristocracy and richly decorated helmets — the immediate precursor to the Viking Age.

920.name: Swedish Viking Age & Varangians
920.description: Swedish Vikings (Varangians) pioneered the eastern route — through Russia to Constantinople and Baghdad — founding the Rus' state, serving as the Byzantine Emperor's elite Varangian Guard, and establishing vast trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Varangians & the Foundation of Rus'
sub_clusters.description: Swedish Vikings sailing east via the river systems of Russia, the semi-legendary Rurik's founding of the Rus' state at Novgorod (862), and the establishment of the trade route 'from the Varangians to the Greeks' linking Scandinavia to Byzantium.
key_events: Varangian Rus' establish trading settlements along the rivers from the Baltic to the Black Sea and Constantinople (9th century)
